newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm ahead of FOMC, on London Club.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm ahead of FOMC, on London Club.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Wednesday, as the market was confident about the unlikelihood of a U.S. interest rate hike.
Traders said the sixth tranche found support after Vneshekonombank chairman Andrei Kostin said Russia expected to close agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors in autumn.
"Buying started in the sixth tranche after the (London Club) news," an International Moscow Bank dealer said. "But generally, the market is paying more attention to news about U.S. interest rates."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets for the second day on Wednesday to consider interest rate policy.
MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"A rate hike is doubtful but it does not mean the market is bullish now," one dealer said. "Profit-taking can start at any level. For instance, right after any FOMC decision."
